The vulnerable code path is absent from the shipped cyrus-sasl2 artifacts. CVE-2026-132138 is a NULL pointer dereference in the SCRAM server when a client sends channel-binding data although the server has no channel-binding configured. The fix is upstream commit 45d66335a4a6a59ef07b6fe8f94ac843c1fd3b86 (https://github.com/cyrusimap/cyrus-sasl/commit/45d66335a4a6a59ef07b6fe8f94ac843c1fd3b86), which adds a NULL check on the server channel-binding type before it is dereferenced in plugins/scram.c. That check is present in the cyrus-sasl 2.1.28 source that Debian packages, and the built libscram plugin in the shipped libsasl2-modules package contains its error message. See https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-132138

Upstream GCC commit 5d419c69ce2e6b86d7da75f18736904885674219 (PR libstdc++/124370) stops std::bitset wide-character stream extraction from sizing its buffer without sizeof(wchar_t). The fix is backported to Debian's gcc-14 14.2.0-19 source for trixie, re-expressed against the 14.2.0 operator>>. Debian trixie has not published the fix; see https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-115455

Upstream GCC commit 2fd8866591b5aea7098835f80ab7e176382175ae makes std::vector<bool> constructors check the element count against max_size() before sizing the bit array, so the word count cannot wrap. The fix is backported to Debian's gcc-14 14.2.0-19 source for trixie, without the from_range constructor hunk, which GCC 14.2.0 does not have. Debian trixie has not published the fix; see https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-114691

Upstream GCC commit c1f32b67510f6f9998deadaef5090b6663adb979 sizes the parallel std::search border table one element larger so the border computation cannot index past it. The vulnerable SRP plugin source is absent from the shipped cyrus-sasl2 artifacts. Debian builds cyrus-sasl2 with SRP disabled (--disable-srp, --disable-srp-setpass), and the built libsasl2-2, libsasl2-modules and libsasl2-modules-gssapi-mit packages contain no SRP module and no SRP strings. DHI backport of upstream gh-150751 (python/cpython commits 2eb2af805c156ca52b316bb4ced5e0ab3971d0ae and 9f52b443c002cccfb54bda0706a9276b6b4a109d) applied to 3.10.22 through 3.15.2. http.client validates the Content-Length header as decimal digits only (RFC 9112 1*DIGIT), ignoring optional spaces or tabs around the value; a value with a sign, an underscore, or an embedded space is not used as the body length. Chunk sizes are validated as hexadecimal digits (RFC 9112 1*HEXDIG, 0-9, a-f and A-F), so valid upper- and lower-case hex chunk sizes are accepted, while a sign, a 0x prefix, an underscore or leading whitespace is rejected instead of being parsed with int(value, 16).

Debian security tracker: fixed in unstable by the same change as CVE-2026-85091, which is upstream zlib commit df84af25dc1942490e1d1c899a07619152a46148. That change resets the stream input pointer and available input after a failed write() in gz_write(), so a later gz* write cannot use the stale caller buffer. This package build includes an adaptation of that upstream change for the zlib 1.3.1 code base. See https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-76844
